# FALCON: A Model and Dataset Agnostic Framework for Synthetic Data Generation for NL2SQL Pairs

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#falcon-synthesis)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.03625v1) · arXiv v1, 2 October 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 32 pages: main sections 1–8, limitations; Appendices A.1–A.12, generation/filtering prompts and examples. Figure 4/5 performance plots visually inspected; tables and pipeline figures fully read.

## Research question

Synthetic SQL training data can be structurally simple, linguistically repetitive or incorrectly aligned, while discarding every ambiguous question removes useful alternative-interpretation supervision.

## Method

FALCON interleaves persona and reserved-word seeding, generates executable SQL then candidate questions, and combines a learned alignment filter with prompt-based screening. An Ambrosia-trained ambiguity scorer triggers generation and validation of a second interpretation. Implemented queries use SQLite.

## Evaluation

Generation/filtering ablations, small human-rated samples and Qwen 1.5B/3B fine-tuning compare synthetic, Spider and mixed data. The ambiguity pipeline is audited on 100 examples. Downstream measures include raw string match, string similarity and result-overlap scores, with difficulty-stratified plots.

## What the results support

The ambiguity audit reports 94% accuracy but only 28.6% recall and 66.7% precision. Synthetic-only training improves harder-query slices while losing aggregate Spider performance; the 3B result-overlap score is 0.32 versus 0.42 for Spider training. Mixing 5% Spider restores much of string-match performance.

## Limits and qualifications

High specificity does not imply complete ambiguity coverage. Complexity and linguistic richness are weighted proxies, and partial result overlap is not semantic correctness. Mixed-model execution results are absent. The 1.5B setup supplies gold-query tables, making it different from unrestricted schema selection. Cost savings are estimated from assumed throughput and prices. Human subsets are described as disjoint, leaving inter-rater reliability unclear.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A relevant synthesis approach for retaining some semantic alternatives in training data, with evidence for controlled complexity coverage rather than demonstrated clarification or abstention capability.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| Claim or inference examined | Original evidence | Location | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 94% ambiguity accuracy means ambiguity is reliably recovered. | The same audit reports 28.6% recall, 66.7% precision and 40% F1; high accuracy is compatible with missing most positives. | §5.3 and Table 3 | Report recall and precision alongside accuracy. |
| Synthetic data improves overall real-benchmark accuracy. | For 3B, Spider Soft-EX is 0.32 under FALCON-only training versus 0.42 under Spider training; gains are concentrated in harder slices. Mixed Soft-EX is not reported. | Table 7; Figure 4 | Qualify to complexity-stratified improvement; do not claim universal transfer. |
| The 16-fold cost reduction is measured end to end. | Appendix A.4 estimates token counts, retention and throughput and applies spot/API prices rather than reporting a controlled timed comparison. | §6.2; Appendix A.4 | Describe as a scenario estimate, not measured benchmark cost. |
